title: Python (standard library only, floor 3.11, Windows/macOS/Linux)

rules.rule: Pass an explicit encoding to every text open, Path.read_text/write_text and text-mode subprocess call: "utf-8" for files this code writes, "utf-8-sig" for JSON/TOML read from a user repo, "utf-8" with errors="replace" when scanning arbitrary repo text. Never rely on the default.
rules.why: On 3.11-3.14 the default is the locale encoding (cp1252 and friends on Windows), and launching with -I ignores PYTHONUTF8, so a missing encoding mangles or crashes on non-ASCII paths and content on Windows only. 3.15 made UTF-8 the default, so the CI 3.x job passes the same code: only the 3.11 Windows job can catch the omission.
rules.repoConvention: Every read/write in scripts/ and tests/ already names its encoding; utf-8-sig is used for user-repo JSON (profile.py, guard.py, pack.py load). Keep it.
rules.until: the floor reaches 3.15 (still recommended after: the 3.15 notes advise an explicit encoding for cross-version code)

rules.rule: Read hook or tool input from sys.stdin.buffer and decode it yourself ("utf-8-sig"); reconfigure sys.stdout/sys.stderr to UTF-8 at the entry point. Do not read sys.stdin in text mode or depend on PYTHONIOENCODING.
rules.why: On Windows, pipes use the ANSI code page, and -I ignores PYTHONIOENCODING. A Cyrillic or accented file path in the hook event would decode wrongly, no longer match its glob, and the guard would allow an edit it should deny.

rules.rule: Write files into a user repo atomically and LF-only: tempfile.mkstemp in the destination folder, os.fdopen(..., encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"), os.replace onto the target, and unlink the temp file on any exception. Do not use a fixed, predictable temp name, and do not write with newline=None.
rules.why: newline=None translates \n to \r\n on Windows, so the same content hashes and diffs differently per OS. A plain write that is interrupted leaves a truncated manifest or rulebook. A fixed temp name such as .<name>.tmp can be pre-planted, for example as a symlink in a cloned repo, and it is left behind on failure. mkstemp creates its file with O_EXCL and is readable only by its creator.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/pack.py main (render --out uses a fixed .<name>.tmp and no cleanup)

rules.rule: Keep the code runnable on 3.11. Do not call APIs added later: Path.walk, Path.with_segments, relative_to(walk_up=), Path.exists(follow_symlinks=), glob/rglob(case_sensitive=) (3.12); PurePath.full_match, read_text(newline=), re.PatternError, os.path.isreserved (3.13); Path.copy/move/info (3.14); NamedTemporaryFile(delete_on_close=), TemporaryDirectory(delete=), shutil.rmtree(onexc=) (3.12). Use re.error, os.walk, and rmtree(onerror=) while the floor is 3.11.
rules.why: Each one raises TypeError or AttributeError on 3.11. The CI 3.x job and a newer local Python both pass, so the break shows up only in the 3.11 matrix job, and only if a test reaches that line. Untested hook code would fail open in users' sessions.
rules.until: the floor in scripts/stackfoundry.sh, .githooks/pre-commit and ci.yml moves past the version that added the API

rules.rule: Run external programs with an argv list, never shell=True. Resolve the executable to an absolute path from absolute PATH entries only, and do not use a bare name or, on 3.11, shutil.which. To relaunch Python, use [sys.executable, "-I", ...].
rules.why: On Windows, CreateProcess and shutil.which before 3.12 can resolve a bare name from the current directory. Here the current directory is an untrusted user repo, so a planted git.exe would run. shell=True adds quoting and injection risk, and .bat/.cmd files go through cmd.exe whatever arguments are passed.
rules.repoConvention: gitutil.git_exe scans PATH itself instead of calling shutil.which (3.11 floor). Keep it while the floor is below 3.12.

rules.rule: When a value from the command line or a profile becomes a git revision argument (--base, --range), put --end-of-options before it, or reject values that start with '-'. Put -- before path arguments.
rules.why: A value such as --output=<file> is parsed as a git option. Through `git diff` it writes a file, which breaks the read-only promise of change-targets and select-tests. Other values change what git lists, so the change set comes out wrong.

rules.rule: To decide whether a path lies inside a root, compare resolved paths component-wise (Path.is_relative_to on resolved paths, or os.path.commonpath). Never use str.startswith or os.path.commonprefix. Fold case and Unicode normalization on both Windows and macOS before matching a path against a glob.
rules.why: commonprefix and startswith work character by character, so /repo-evil passes as being inside /repo. PurePosixPath compares case-sensitively, but the default macOS APFS volume is case-insensitive and normalization-insensitive, and Windows is case-insensitive. A Write to gen/FOO.json, or an NFD spelling of a name, reaches the same file but misses a case-sensitive glob, and the guard fails open.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py _relative (lower() on Windows only; globs.match is case-sensitive)

rules.rule: Convert a path to forward slashes (Path.as_posix() or .replace("\\", "/")) before it is globbed, hashed, stored in JSON or printed for other tools. Remember that os.path.normpath returns backslashes on Windows and can change the meaning of a path that contains symlinks.
rules.why: A backslash path matches no profile glob and is stored under a second key in manifest.lock.json. The same repo then gets different results on Windows than on macOS or Linux.

rules.rule: Validate the shape of parsed JSON/TOML from a user repo (isinstance checks before .get, indexing or iteration). At the CLI boundary, map only expected errors to exit 2 (OSError, ValueError, which covers JSONDecodeError, TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError, plus the repo's own error types). Never let an AttributeError, TypeError or KeyError escape as a traceback.
rules.why: json and tomllib return whatever the file holds. `project = "x"` in a pyproject.toml makes project.get raise AttributeError. That error is not mapped, so the process dies with a traceback and a nonzero status, which a caller can read as 1 = 'ran and found something', and survey output stops for the whole repo.

rules.rule: In a fail-open hook, catch Exception (not BaseException) around the whole decision and print nothing on error. Make every input the hook would silently skip (bad regex, missing key, invalid JSON) reportable through a separate check command.
rules.why: A crash that blocks the hook wedges the user's session. A silent skip turns a deny rule into an allow without anyone noticing.
rules.repoConvention: guard.main wraps decide() in `except Exception` (noqa BLE001) and guard --check reports skipped rules. This is the only sanctioned broad except, together with checks.today.

rules.rule: Give every subprocess.run that a hook, an agent or a test waits on a timeout, and catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired as a could-not-run error. When a command runs in a different repo from the caller, strip the variables listed by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE...) from env.
rules.why: With no timeout, a hung git hangs the CLI indefinitely. run() kills the child only when a timeout is set. Git exports GIT_DIR and related variables to hooks, so tests run from .githooks/pre-commit that call git in a temporary repo can act on the outer repository instead.
where: tests/_support.py git, run_cli (timeout=120, env inherits os.environ)

rules.rule: Keep re.match / Pattern.match. Do not switch to re.prefixmatch until the floor is 3.15.
rules.why: prefixmatch exists only from 3.15, and match is soft-deprecated with no planned removal. Switching early breaks every job older than 3.15.

bugCategories.name: implicit-locale-encoding
bugCategories.lookFor: open(), read_text(), write_text(), TextIOWrapper, or subprocess text=True without encoding=; sys.stdin read in text mode; json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False) printed to a stream that was not reconfigured.
bugCategories.failure: Mojibake or UnicodeDecodeError on Windows with non-ASCII paths (the repo owner's own path is Cyrillic). The guard misses a protected file; survey drops or corrupts manifests.

bugCategories.name: newer-than-floor-api
bugCategories.lookFor: Any API with an 'Added in' or 'Changed in' note of 3.12 or later (see the floor rule) on a code path the 3.11 job does not exercise.
bugCategories.failure: AttributeError or TypeError on users' Python 3.11. In the hook this fails open silently; in the CLI it gives exit 2 or a traceback.

bugCategories.name: path-identity-mismatch
bugCategories.lookFor: String comparison of paths, startswith or commonprefix for containment, a case fold only when os.name == 'nt', no Unicode normalization, backslashes reaching globs or JSON keys, or normpath used before a symlink-sensitive decision.
bugCategories.failure: The guard allows an edit to a generated file reached through a different case, an NFD name or a '..' route. Duplicate manifest entries, or change sets that miss files, on one OS only.

bugCategories.name: argv-injection-into-git
bugCategories.lookFor: A user- or profile-supplied string placed in a git argv slot without --end-of-options or --; f-strings building a revision from input.
bugCategories.failure: git reads the value as an option: a read-only subcommand writes a file (git diff --output) or lists the wrong change set.

bugCategories.name: non-atomic-or-crlf-write
bugCategories.lookFor: write_text or open('w') straight onto a file in the user repo; newline left at None; a fixed temp name; a temp file not removed on exception.
bugCategories.failure: A truncated manifest.lock.json or rulebook after an interrupt, CRLF on Windows that changes hashes, or a stray .tmp file.

bugCategories.name: unchecked-parsed-shape
bugCategories.lookFor: Chained .get() calls or [] on json.loads/tomllib.loads results from user files without isinstance checks; except clauses that cover only ValueError.
bugCategories.failure: Traceback and an ambiguous exit status on a malformed but parseable manifest; one bad file aborts the survey of a whole repo.

bugCategories.name: swallowed-error
bugCategories.lookFor: `except Exception` or a bare except outside the sanctioned fail-open points (guard.main, checks.today); except blocks that return a default with no report; os.walk without onerror where a missing subtree matters.
bugCategories.failure: Wrong output reported as success: a guard rule silently skipped, a survey that omits unreadable folders without saying so.

bugCategories.name: unbounded-subprocess-or-input
bugCategories.lookFor: subprocess.run without timeout; inherited GIT_* env when running git against another repo; json/tomllib parsing of user files with no size cap; regexes from guards.json run on every command.
bugCategories.failure: A hung hook or CLI, git acting on the wrong repository during pre-commit, or CPU/memory exhaustion from a crafted manifest.

testing.layers: unittest only. In-process tests call module functions such as guard.decide and survey.survey on TempRepo trees. Subprocess tests run the real entry point with `python -I` through run_cli, which proves the launcher contract: isolated mode, stdin bytes and exit codes. Prove cross-platform path and encoding behaviour with non-ASCII and mixed-case file names in TempRepo, because the CI matrix runs Windows, macOS and Linux on 3.11 and 3.x.
harness: tests/_support.py TempRepo, write, git, run_cli, HAS_GIT
tests/__init__.py (makes tests/ a regular package for discovery)
testing.shuffle: unittest has no random order: tests run sorted by method name. Keep each test self-contained in its own TempRepo rather than relying on order.
testing.mutation: No mutation tool in this repo; this belongs to a tooling pack, not this one.
traps: A missing encoding= passes on the 3.x job (3.15 defaults to UTF-8) and on Linux/macOS. Only the 3.11 Windows job catches it, so put a non-ASCII path in any test that touches I/O.
tomllib parses TOML 1.1 from 3.15 (multi-line inline tables, trailing commas, \e and \xHH escapes). A test that expects such input to be 'invalid TOML' passes on 3.11 and fails on 3.x.
argparse output differs across the matrix: 3.14 can colour help, and 3.15 turns suggest_on_error on by default. Do not assert on full help or error text, only on exit codes and key phrases.
tests/__init__.py must stay: on 3.11-3.13, discovery ignores namespace packages.
skipUnless(HAS_GIT) or a missing sh skips silently. A green local run without git proves nothing about the gitutil paths.
Tests that call git in a TempRepo inherit the environment. Run from .githooks/pre-commit, GIT_DIR and related variables can point at the outer repo, so clear them in _support.git.
On Windows, TemporaryDirectory cleanup raises PermissionError if a file inside is still open. Close handles, including subprocess pipes, before leaving the with block.
From 3.15, assertWarns no longer swallows non-matching warnings, so a test can start failing only on the 3.x job.

performance.note: Cap the size of user-repo files before json.loads or tomllib.loads (both docs advise limiting input size), as survey already does for generated-marker scans (GENERATED_MAX_SIZE). survey._read reads every manifest whole.

Prefer git ls-files -z over a filesystem walk, and keep os.walk at followlinks=False (the default) with symlinked directories pruned. walk() does not track visited directories, so following links can loop forever.

security.note: Always launch with -I. It keeps the script directory and user site-packages off sys.path and ignores PYTHON* variables, so a module planted in the user's repo is never imported. The cost is that PYTHONUTF8 and PYTHONIOENCODING are ignored too, hence the explicit-encoding rules. Add only this package's own parent to sys.path.

Patterns in guards.json are compiled with re. re has no match timeout and documents no limit on backtracking, so a catastrophic pattern stalls every Bash/PowerShell tool call. guard --check should flag nested quantifiers. Possessive quantifiers and atomic groups are available from 3.11 when a pattern needs them.

3.11 is security-only until 2027-10. The August 2026 security releases (3.11.16) limit the number of key parts in tomllib, and survey parses untrusted pyproject.toml and Cargo.toml with it. CVE-2026-12003 (Windows legacy all-users installer, sys.path landmark outside the install directory) affects 3.11.15 and earlier. Tell users to run the newest 3.11.x or a newer Python.

pins: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh: ok() sys.version_info >= (3, 11) and the error message
lockStep: The three pins above move together, together with the prose floor in .claude/CLAUDE.md ('Python 3.11+') and .claude/rules/authoring.md ('Python >= 3.11').
Raising the floor unlocks the APIs in the floor rule (3.12: Path.walk, rmtree onexc, NamedTemporaryFile delete_on_close; 3.13: re.PatternError, full_match; 3.15: re.prefixmatch, UTF-8 default).
deprecationsInUse: re.match / Pattern.match: soft-deprecated in 3.15 in favour of prefixmatch, with no removal planned. Used in globs.py, survey.py, tracker.py, frontmatter.py, pack.py and others; keep it while the floor is below 3.15.

from __future__ import annotations: not deprecated yet. PEP 749 deprecates it no sooner than the first release after 3.13's end of life (2029-10). Used at the top of every module in scripts/stackfoundry and tests/_support.py.

notReached: GitHub security advisories for python/cpython (https://github.com/python/cpython/security/advisories) listed no advisories, possibly because of a filter. CPython advisories were taken from the security-announce list and the python.org blog instead, from a single search, so the coverage may be incomplete.

The removed/deprecated sections of What's New in 3.15 past character 200000, and the 3.14 notes past character 100000, were truncated. Entries there for subprocess, tempfile, io and zoneinfo were not read.
What's New in 3.12 and 3.13 were not read in full. Their API additions are cited from the per-module 'Added/Changed in version' notes instead.
The exit status of an uncaught exception is not stated in the sys docs that were read. The unchecked-parsed-shape rule assumes a nonzero status that callers cannot distinguish (see questions).
questions: pack.py main (render --out) writes through a fixed '.<name>.tmp' with write_text and does not clean up on failure, while manifest.write_json uses mkstemp, os.replace and cleanup. Should render switch to the write_json pattern?

change-targets/select-tests pass --range and --base values to git unguarded (`--range=--output=<file>` would make `git diff` write a file). Should resolve_files and changed_files add --end-of-options or reject a leading '-'?

guard._relative folds case only when os.name == 'nt', and globs.match is case-sensitive. On a default (case-insensitive) macOS volume, and with NFD names, a generated file reached through another spelling is not denied. Should the guard fold case and NFC-normalize on macOS too?

gitutil.run has no timeout, and tests/_support.git passes os.environ through, including GIT_DIR and related variables when run from .githooks/pre-commit. Add a timeout, and strip the --local-env-vars set for git calls in temporary repos?

cli.main maps only ProfileError, GitError, OSError and ValueError to exit 2. A malformed-but-parseable manifest (e.g. `project = "x"`) raises AttributeError in survey.parse_pyproject and exits with a traceback. Should main also map unexpected exceptions to 2, or should the parsers validate shape?
With Python 3.11 reaching end of life in 2027-10, when should the floor move? The pins and the lock-step prose are listed under upgrade.
